thought_title: The Christian way of life is not a human invention but a revelation from the Creator himself
orientation: The author has just described the Christians' remarkable place in the world and now explains that their way of life was not devised by human beings but was revealed and established by God himself, who sent his Son not to terrify but to save.
pass_a_gloss: For not an earthly discovery, as I said, was this handed over to them, nor do they deem it right to guard a mortal thought so carefully, nor have they been entrusted with a stewardship of human mysteries. But he himself truly, the Almighty and Creator of all and invisible God, he himself from heaven established the truth and the holy and incomprehensible Word (the Son, Christ; the same figure also called Son and only-begotten) among human beings and fixed it in their hearts: not, as someone might suppose, sending to human beings some servant or angel or ruler or one of those who administer earthly things or one of those entrusted with the administrations in heaven, but the very craftsman and maker of all things, by whom he created the heavens, by whom he enclosed the sea with its own bounds, whose mysteries all the elements faithfully guard, from whom the sun has received the measures of the courses of the day to guard, whom the moon obeys when he commands it to shine by night, whom the stars obey, following the course of the moon: by whom all things have been ordered and determined and subjected, the heavens and the things in the heavens, the earth and the things in the earth, the sea and the things in the sea, fire, air, abyss, the things in the heights, the things in the depths, the things in between: this one he sent to them. Surely not, as someone might reason in human terms, for tyranny and fear and terror? By no means: but in gentleness and meekness, as a king sending a son, a king, he sent him, as God he sent him, as a human being to human beings he sent him, as saving he sent him, as persuading, not using force: for force is not present in God. He sent him as calling, not pursuing: he sent him as loving, not judging. For he will send him as judge: and who will endure his coming? ... thrown to wild beasts, so that they may deny the Lord, and not being conquered? Do you not see that the more numerous are punished, the more numerous others increase? These things do not seem to be the works of a human being: these things are the power of God: these things are the proofs of his coming.

lemmas.gloss: being thrown to, being exposed to

choices.why: οἰκονομία here means an entrusted administration or stewardship, and μυστηρίων is the object of that stewardship; the phrase contrasts human religious systems with what God himself has revealed.

choices.term: τὸν λόγον τὸν ἅγιον καὶ ἀπερινόητον
choices.why: λόγος is capitalized as Word per the glossary, referring to the divine Son; ἀπερινόητον means beyond human comprehension, not merely 'unthinkable'.
Both nouns describe the manner of God's sending; ἐπιείκεια is gentleness or fairness, πραΰτης is meekness or mildness, and the pair contrasts with tyranny, fear, and terror.

choices.term: ὡς βασιλεὺς πέμπων υἱὸν βασιλέα ἔπεμψεν
choices.english: as a king sending a son, a king, he sent him
choices.why: The repetition of βασιλεύς is deliberate: the sender is a king and the one sent is also a king; the rendering preserves the double royal status.
rejected: as a king sending his son the king he sent him
as a king he sent a kingly son

choices.term: βία γὰρ οὐ πρόσεστι τῷ θεῷ
choices.english: for force is not present in God
choices.why: πρόσεστι means 'is present in' or 'belongs to'; the point is that force has no place in God's nature, not merely that God does not use force.
rejected: for violence is not in God

choices.why: δείγματα are visible proofs or tokens; παρουσία is rendered 'coming' per the glossary, referring to the Son's presence and future coming.

pass_b_english: For this way of life was not handed down to them as an earthly discovery, as I said. Nor do they think it worth guarding so carefully as a merely human idea. Nor have they been entrusted with a stewardship of human mysteries.

No. The invisible God himself, the Almighty and Creator of all, established from heaven among human beings the truth and the holy and incomprehensible Word, and fixed him firmly in their hearts. He did not, as someone might suppose, send to human beings some servant, or an angel, or a ruler, or one of those who administer earthly affairs, or one of those entrusted with the governments in the heavens. He sent the very Craftsman and Maker of all things, by whom he created the heavens, by whom he shut up the sea within its own bounds, whose mysteries all the elements faithfully keep, from whom the sun has received the measures of the day's courses to keep, whom the moon obeys when he commands it to shine by night, whom the stars obey as they follow the course of the moon. By him all things have been ordered, and marked out, and made subject: the heavens and the things in the heavens, the earth and the things in the earth, the sea and the things in the sea, fire, air, the abyss, the things in the heights, the things in the depths, the things in between. This is the one he sent to them.
Did he send him, as a human being might reason, for tyranny and fear and terror?

Not at all. He sent him in gentleness and meekness. As a king sending a son, a king, he sent him. As God he sent him. As a human being to human beings he sent him. As one who saves he sent him. As one who persuades, not one who uses force, for force is not present in God.
He sent the Son as one who calls, not one who pursues. He sent the Son as one who loves, not one who judges.
For he will send the Son as judge, and who will endure his coming?

Do you not see those thrown to wild beasts, that they might deny the Lord, yet are not conquered? Do you not see that the more are punished, the more others increase? These do not seem to be the works of a human being. These are the power of God. These are the proofs of his coming.
notes: The text has a lacuna after 'καὶ τίς αὐτοῦ τὴν παρουσίαν ὑποστήσεται;' where the source resumes mid-sentence with 'παραβαλλομένους θηρίοις...' The gloss reflects the break without inventing missing text.
